chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, who said:
I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the prayer of the supererogatory tawaf after ʿAṣr, and he said: No.

So I mentioned to him the statement of some of his forefathers: The people did not take anything from al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام except the prayer after ʿAṣr in Makkah. He said: Yes, but when you see the people turning toward something, then avoid it. I said: These people do it. He said: You are not like them.

key_terms.الْحَسَنِ: Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, cited as part of the transmitted precedent
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ: Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, cited alongside Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام
key_terms.بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ: the time after the ʿAṣr prayer, relevant to the ruling
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: in Makkah, specifying the location of the mentioned practice
key_terms.صَلَاةِ: the ritual prayer being discussed in legal context
key_terms.طَوَافِ: circumambulation of the Kaʿbah, for which a prayer is performed
key_terms.فَاجْتَنِبْهُ: avoid it, expressing the Imam's directive

ai.seo_question: Can the prayer of supererogatory tawaf be performed after ʿAṣr according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on performing the two rakʿahs of a supererogatory tawaf after ʿAṣr. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام forbids it in this report and distinguishes the conduct of the Shīʿah from that of others, while acknowledging a transmitted practice connected to al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام in Makkah.
